subject: Qualify: latency & throughput bottlenecks — KPI matrix request
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Arthur Blake <arthur@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: latency & throughput discovery — KPI matrix request

Arthur / team — thanks again for the tight 30-minute intro today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points you described:
- Streaming UX: partial tokens sometimes arrive delayed which degrades real-time editor experience.
- P95 latency spikes during burst windows (current p95 observed ~420ms, target <=180ms).
- Concurrency: bursty simultaneous sessions during peak marketing campaigns (~200–300 concurrent sessions).
- Occasional backend OOMs when sequence lengths spike.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Model serving: 3rd-party managed endpoints (pay-per-request) with limited batching control.
- Frontend: live-collab editor relying on streaming tokens.
- Auth/data: requests include per-session user context, KV store for short-term chat history.

Success criteria you listed:
1) P95 <= 180ms for first-token on typical prompt mix.
2) Streaming token delivery with <50ms inter-token jitter for average responses.
3) Sustained concurrency up to 250 sessions with graceful degradation and clear fallback.

What we need from you to size and propose an initial config:
- Filled KPI matrix (attached) with traffic profile: per-minute request distribution, average and 95th percentile prompt lengths, and peak concurrency windows.
- Sample anonymized logs or a small load trace (CSV) that shows token lengths / response time distribution.
- Any hard SSO or compliance constraints for private deploy (if you need VPC/HSM).

Attachments: kpi-request-template.xlsx (one-sheet template; please fill the highlighted cells).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Please return the filled KPI matrix + sample trace by EOD Thu, Dec 3.
- We’ll run an initial sizing and share a recommended config + expected cost and latency profile by Fri, Dec 4.
- Technical deep-dive (1 hour) to align on integration & canary plan — proposed: Thu, Dec 3 09:00 PT.

If that schedule looks tight for your team, tell us which day next week works and we’ll adapt.

Thanks — looking forward to the matrix so we can validate whether Dedicated or Private makes more sense for you.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0129
https://redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Arthur Blake <arthur@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency & throughput discovery — KPI matrix request

Thanks Steph — solid summary. A couple of quick additions from an SE perspective before the deep-dive: 
- Please ask Acme to include tokenization distribution (tokens per user input and tokens per generated response) — that's often where we see unexpected long tails.
- If you can provide 95th percentile prompt length and the distribution over time (hourly), we can model batching benefits more accurately.
- Proposed test: a 1-hour canary with synthetic traffic that mirrors the CSV sample to validate p95 and streaming jitter; we'll bring an engineer to instrument KV cache hit metrics.

I can prepare the canary run template and ops checklist once we have the matrix. Happy to present during the deep-dive.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Arthur Blake <arthur@acme.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency & throughput discovery — KPI matrix request

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the recap and the template. We’ll fill out the KPI matrix and attach a small load trace.

Attached: acme-load-sample.csv (anonymized sample of 2 hours of traffic; contains timestamp, token_count_in, token_count_out, observed_latency_ms).

Dec 3 at 09:00 PT works for our infra lead (Jordan) and me. One question: will the deep-dive include a discussion of streaming protocol (SSE vs WebSocket) options? We currently use SSE and have seen the jitter there.

I’ll get the matrix back to you by EOD Dec 3.

Best —
Arthur

arthur@acme.ai

Great — thanks Arthur, and thanks Ben. Dec 3, 09:00 PT is confirmed. Calendar invite & meeting link below.

Meet: https://redwood.app/meet/stephanie/acme-deepdive (Dial-in + recording enabled)
Agenda (45–60 mins):

- 20m: Infra deep-dive — p95 analysis, streaming jitter root causes, concurrency modeling (Redwood SEs)
- 15m: Canary plan & success criteria (ops playbook)
- 10m: Action items & next-mile decisions (Dedicated vs Private)

Required attendees: Jordan (Acme infra), Arthur (Acme), Stephanie/Ben/Karthik (Redwood). Optional: Product or Security if you want SLA/compliance discussion.
